13.1 Development Workflow – Overview

The development workflow of the ABpE Portal is designed to add new features quickly and safely, modify existing ones, and deploy the system. The modular design enables parallel development on different components.

13.2 Creating a New Module – Step by Step

The following steps are required to add a new module to the ABpE Portal. The system is designed to require as little manual configuration as possible.

  1. Create module folder:
    mkdir -p apps/abpe_ui/templates/abpe_ui/modules/mein_modul
  2. Create module.json:
    cat > apps/abpe_ui/templates/abpe_ui/modules/mein_modul/module.json << 'EOF'
{
    "id": "mein_modul",
    "title": "Mein Modul",
    "icon": "star",
    "route": "/mein_modul/",
    "order": 50,
    "enabled": true,
    "static": {
        "css": ["mod-mein_modul.css"],
        "js": ["mod-mein_modul.js"]
    }
}
EOF
  3. Create template:
    touch apps/abpe_ui/templates/abpe_ui/modules/mein_modul/index.html
  4. Create CSS/JS (optional):
    touch apps/abpe_ui/static/abpe_ui/css/mod/mod-mein_modul.css
    touch apps/abpe_ui/static/abpe_ui/js/mod/mod-mein_modul.js
  5. Create i18n files:
    touch apps/abpe_ui/static/abpe_ui/i18n/de/modules/mein_modul.json
    touch apps/abpe_ui/static/abpe_ui/i18n/en/modules/mein_modul.json
  6. Collect static files:
    python manage.py collectstatic
  7. The module appears automatically in the sidebar – no further changes needed!

13.3 Modifying an Existing Module

If an existing module is to be modified, the following points must be considered:

  1. Adjust module.json: Change order, icon, activation status
  2. Edit template(s): Adjust HTML structure
  3. Adjust CSS/JS: Module-specific styles and logic
  4. Update i18n: Add new translations
  5. Test: Check functionality and display
  6. Run collectstatic: python manage.py collectstatic

13.4 Development with Docker (optional)

For an isolated development environment, Docker can be used:

# Build container
docker-compose build

# Start container
docker-compose up -d

# Run migrations
docker-compose exec web python manage.py migrate

# Collect static files
docker-compose exec web python manage.py collectstatic

# Run tests
docker-compose exec web python manage.py test

13.5 Deployment

For deployment to the production environment, the following steps are required:

# Collect static files
python manage.py collectstatic --noinput

# Database migrations
python manage.py migrate

# Restart server (Gunicorn)
sudo systemctl restart gunicorn

# Or Apache
sudo systemctl restart apache2

# Restart Celery worker (for asynchronous tasks)
sudo systemctl restart celery

# Clear Redis cache (optional)
redis-cli FLUSHALL

13.6 Best Practices – DO's ✅

  • Each module has its own module.json
  • Use i18n for all texts (data-i18n)
  • Outsource help texts in {module}_help.json
  • CSS only the essentials per module (inherited from global)
  • Use Bootstrap Icons for consistent display
  • Write mobile-first CSS
  • Backup before major changes: python backup_restore.py -save datei.py

13.7 Best Practices – DON'Ts ❌

  • No hardcoded texts in HTML
  • No hardcoded URLs
  • No duplication of global styles
  • No direct DOM manipulations outside of module JS
  • No fixed badge values (always dynamic via API)
  • No changes to views.py or urls.py for new modules (use generic routes!)

13.8 Version Control (Git)

Recommended .gitignore entries for the project:

# Django
*.pyc
__pycache__/
*.log
*.sqlite3
staticfiles/
media/

# Backups
archive/*/apps/
archive/*/templates/
!archive/.gitignore
!archive/README.md

# Environment variables
.env
.venv/

# IDE
.vscode/
.idea/
*.swp
